ledger.notes: Policy statements phrased only as recommendations, including asking for trip details, asking about insurance, helping locate an unknown reservation ID, and refunding a lower cabin-price difference, were not treated as norms under the rubric's required-versus-recommended rule. The one-tool-call-at-a-time and no-simultaneous-response mechanics are harness-format rules and were excluded; several agent blocks combine explanatory text with a tool call, but those mechanics are only noted here. Permissions and constraints governing bookings, modifications, cancellations, refunds, and compensation were treated as conduct norms because this is a policy-governed customer-service dialogue. No unsourced agent-authored conduct rule was identified.

Claims in the generated manual about a placeholder Git repository and an MIT license were not recorded as authored rules because they are artifact-content assertions, not rules governing an agent's conduct. The environment later reports that the software ran successfully and passed testing [T0B113] [T0B114], but these are outcomes rather than norm statements.
